findings.reason: the miss would be attributed to imas-efit's representation, which is exactly the false implication the section's one-directional rule exists to prevent.
findings.text: §6b says "the shell geometry is authored as a new iron-boundary element" (singular), but imas-efit's `IronBoundary` is "a single closed-path iron-air interface" (`src/ironBoundary.h:30-34`), and its own orientation rule — "the inner boundary of the transformer must be defined in a CLOCKWISE direction, whereas the outer boundary must be defined in an ANTI-CLOCKWISE direction" — shows a body with a cavity needs two elements of opposite orientation; one closed contour at radius b is a solid iron sphere of μ<sub>r</sub> = 1000, whose shielding is nowhere near the shell's exact S = 61.10, so a worker following the section literally scores a "miss" for the wrong body

findings.reason: the section's whole verdict hangs on the geometry having been read as intended, and the named control is exactly the one that cannot see a geometry defect, so a mis-wiring and a representation error are indistinguishable in the result.
findings.text: clause (2) offers μ<sub>r</sub> = 1 returning S = 1 as "the control that its shell configuration is wired", but at μ<sub>r</sub> = 1 the exact S is 1 for every geometry, so a boundary authored at the wrong radius, or as a solid body rather than a shell, or read as the wrong material still returns 1 to precision and the control cannot fail

findings.reason: the "a miss cannot be under-resolution" guarantee would be false without an iteration-convergence clause, and an unconverged iron solve would be read as a representation miss.
findings.text: §6b calls `relativeError` "its iteration tolerance ... 1e-2 by default" and tightens it to 1e-6, but the parameter's documented criterion is `2(I_i − I_{i−1})(I_i + I_{i−1}) < relativeError` (`usermanual/xml/ironModel.xml:76-80`), an absolute threshold on the squared change of the summed segment currents and not a relative accuracy, and the shipped `configuration/machines/_common/solver/iron-solver.xml` also caps the solve at `maximumIterationCount="100"` with `relaxFactor="0.5"`; the section states no evidence that 1e-6 is reachable inside that cap, and its only convergence evidence — S moving under 0.5 % under one further refinement — tests resolution, not iteration, so an inner solve that hit the iteration cap is recorded, in the plan's own words, as "converged"

findings.reason: the file is found by one search and its content is as the section describes, so the pointer is mis-pathed but not misleading about the mechanism.
findings.text: the section cites the tolerance default at `_common/solver/iron-solver.xml`, which exists at neither that path nor any path under `configuration/` other than `configuration/machines/_common/solver/iron-solver.xml` (WEST's `iron.xml` includes it as `${EFIT_CONFIG_DIR}/machines/_common/solver/iron-solver.xml`), so the one pointer a worker needs in order to change the value does not resolve as written
